context: This is also the setting of parametrized property testing introduced by Parnas et al [52]. In this setting, a property is parametrized by an integer k and denoted P = {Pk }k . A (k1 , k2 )-tester for the family P is a randomized algorithm which, on input a proximity parameter ε ∈ (0, 1) and oracle access to an unknown function f , must accept if f ∈ Pk1 , with probability at least 2/3; and reject if d(f, Pk2 ) > ε, with probability at least 2/3. Hence, we are interested in (k, g(k, n))-testing for parametrized monotonicity, denoted {Mk }k . Following the notation just described, we will speak of property testers for (and query complexity lower bounds for) (k, g(k, n))-testing the property {Mk }k . √ I Theorem 6. Parametrized monotonicity testing may provide a new angle for approaching yet unanswered questions towards the goal of understanding the role of adaptivity in testing monotonicity. The current strong lower bounds for testing monotonicity adaptively [25, 24, 5] come polynomially close to the one-sided error upper bounds [43], yet the question of whether adaptive algorithms can beat the current lower bounds still remain open. 1.3 Parametrized monotonicity testing on the hypergrid We next study parametrized monotonicity testing of Boolean functions over the hypergrid [n]d domain.
